headline: AI agents book only 4 Uber rides in busiest week, company reveals
summary: Uber's CEO Dara Khosrowshahi stated that AI agents are seeing "very limited traction" for booking rides, despite the growing hype around AI task automation.
details: Uber's CEO Dara Khosrowshahi revealed that during the busiest week of October, only four rides were booked through AI agents. This comes amid significant hype for AI agents capable of performing tasks on users' behalf.

While a slightly higher number of orders were placed via AI agents on Uber Eats, the total was still small. Across both services, Uber handled approximately 320 million trips and orders during the week of Halloween, with only 500 Uber Eats orders placed by AI agents.

Khosrowshahi acknowledged the low adoption, stating "It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far." He expressed hope for increased future usage, while noting that current booking times through the app are already very fast, averaging 50 seconds for rides and 90 seconds for food re-orders.

The low numbers from Uber follow similar reports from other companies. DoorDash recently stated it received only a few hundred orders from AI agents. Despite the current limited adoption, Khosrowshahi remains optimistic about the potential of AI agents to increase demand on their platform.
caption:
AI agents are supposed to automate tasks, but Uber's latest earnings call revealed a surprising lack of adoption.

Uber's CEO Dara Khosrowshahi revealed that during the busiest week of October, only four rides were booked through AI agents. This comes amid significant hype for AI agents capable of performing tasks on users' behalf.

While a slightly higher number of orders were placed via AI agents on Uber Eats, the total was still small. Across both services, Uber handled approximately 320 million trips and orders during the week of Halloween, with only 500 Uber Eats orders placed by AI agents.

Khosrowshahi acknowledged the low adoption, stating "It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far." He expressed hope for increased future usage, while noting that current booking times through the app are already very fast, averaging 50 seconds for rides and 90 seconds for food re-orders.

The low numbers from Uber follow similar reports from other companies. DoorDash recently stated it received only a few hundred orders from AI agents. Despite the current limited adoption, Khosrowshahi remains optimistic about the potential of AI agents to increase demand on their platform.
